note: Directional 2D figures in a 3D shot: the figure is a flat sprite and the drawing that faces the camera is chosen by angle (ui/src/features/scene3d/directionalSprite.ts, services/series_directional.py). Angles are degrees of the figure's facing against the line to the camera: 0 faces the camera, +90 faces screen-right, 180 turns its back. A sheet looks right; the left is its mirror.
walkDiagonal_note: While a figure walks, the part of its movement that is larger decides the sheet: toward or away from the camera (front, back) or across the screen (side). The three-quarter sheets draw only a really diagonal walk, the angles from 45 - walkDiagonalDeg to 45 + walkDiagonalDeg off the line to the camera (and the same from the back). 12 is about 3:2 (a walk 1.5 times more toward the camera than across it is still a front walk); 22.5 gives every sector the same width as for a figure that stands, 0 turns the three-quarter sheets off while walking. walkHysteresisDeg is how far past an edge a walking figure keeps its sheet (a straight walk crosses each edge once, so it can be small). A kit with no three-quarter sheet for the motion splits that band at 45 (or 135) degrees, so the larger part of the movement still decides.
lateral_note: A kit may also draw the other side of a lateral direction as its own sheet: dir side_r, front34_r or back34_r looks left and beats the mirror.
